logline: Released after 18 years in prison for his sister Sara's murder, Alex Guzman sets out to destroy the wealthy Lazcano family he holds responsible - only to find the truth is far worse than anyone's lie.

bollymeter.basis: Season 1 holds 86% on Rotten Tomatoes from 7 critics. Netflix reported the series was watched by 55 million households in its first 28 days, making it the platform's most-watched non-English title at that point. IMDb series rating is 6.4.

pull_quotes.text: An entertaining thriller with the soul of a telenovela that mixes mystery, drama and eroticism.
Has a few logic problems, but its overall vibe is energetic enough, with good performances, to keep viewers' attention.

seasons.review_body: Season 1 landed March 24, 2021 and immediately became a global Netflix phenomenon - the platform later reported 55 million household views in the first 28 days and 266 million hours watched, making it the most-watched non-English title on the service at that point. Critics scored it 86 percent from 7 reviews: Espinof called it an entertaining thriller with the soul of a telenovela; El Pais praised how subscription TV had allowed Mexican melodrama to flourish luxuriously. Decider acknowledged logic problems but found the energetic vibe and committed performances sufficient. The audience-versus-critic split visible in the IMDb rating of 6.4 reflects the show's nature: it operates on telenovela mechanics, not prestige-drama logic, and rewards audiences who understand the register.

episode_reviews.title: Episode 1
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The premiere deploys its premise with unusual efficiency: Alex's release, the flashback to Sara's death, and the establishment of the Lazcano family as the target all land in the first episode. The show is upfront about being a revenge thriller rather than a slow-burn mystery, and the tonal clarity is an asset.
episode_reviews.the_moment: Alex's first return to the location where Sara died - the show's governing obsession is established here, and Manolo Cardona's contained fury is immediately compelling.

critic_note.text: The series progresses with remarkable fluidity, supported by a constant bet on the surefire tropes of the telenovela.

bollymeter.basis: Season 2 dropped to 37% on Rotten Tomatoes from 2 critics. The New York Times' Mike Hale wrote that waiting to see if theories pan out tests patience - a pointed critique of a mystery that kept expanding rather than resolving.

pull_quotes.text: This can wear at your patience while you wait to see if your own pet theory turns out to be right.

seasons.review_body: Season 2 arrived just eight weeks after Season 1, released May 19, 2021. The speed of turnaround signalled Netflix's confidence in the IP after the first season's record viewership, but the critical response fell sharply to 37 percent from 2 reviews. The core problem was structural: Season 2 expanded the mystery rather than resolving it, introducing new conspiracies and characters when the audience had invested in getting an answer. Mike Hale at the New York Times identified the central failure precisely - the show's patience-testing delay mechanics worked in Season 1 because the premise was new; by Season 2, the same techniques read as stalling. Espinof maintained that the show's direct approach to even its absurdities kept it watchable, but the consensus tracked downward.
seasons.season_over_season: Drops from telenovela-pleasure to frustration as Season 2 multiplies mystery threads without delivering on Season 1's promise of answers.

bollymeter.basis: Season 3 registered 23% on Rotten Tomatoes from 1 review. Ready Steady Cut found the truth about Sara delivered via a strained conspiracy that added unnecessary scale to what could have been a cleaner resolution.

pull_quotes.text: The show finally reaches the truth but does so with a strained story making a larger, not needed conspiracy.

seasons.review_body: Season 3 wrapped the series May 18, 2022 with Sara's murder finally given an answer after 25 total episodes. The resolution came with the series' worst critical score - 23 percent from one review - and Ready Steady Cut's assessment captured the problem: the show had expanded the conspiracy to a scale that the finale could not satisfyingly pay off. The truth turned out to be both simpler and stranger than three seasons of misdirection suggested, and the pivot toward larger institutional forces felt engineered rather than earned. Viewers who persisted through Seasons 2 and 3 primarily for closure received it, but the gap between the first season's audience explosion and the finale's critical reception measures the distance the show traveled in the wrong direction.
seasons.season_over_season: Delivers closure on Sara's murder but via conspiracy scaffolding that collapsed under its own weight - the finale season is the weakest of the three.
